strengths: Strong specific metrics throughout: ~100 users scaling to 300+, tens of thousands of documents, Fortune-200 biopharma client
Cover letter opens with a compelling, specific story about RTF document processing that demonstrates hands-on experience
Clear research into Pocket's business model (AI Front Office for rehab therapy, scheduling/intake/documentation)
Resume is well-structured with relevant technical skills (RAG, vector DBs, embeddings, agent architecture)
Domain transition from biopharma to rehab therapy is acknowledged thoughtfully
weaknesses: Cover letter has some over-structured, slightly AI-influenced phrasing (e.g., 'what drew me to Pocket's AI Engineer role', 'maps closely to what Pocket is tackling')
Resume bullets describe activities but lack outcome metrics (e.g., efficiency gains, error reduction, time saved)
The biopharma-to-rehab-therapy transition is acknowledged but the gap in clinical operations experience isn't fully addressed
Some cover letter sentences are quite long and structured in ways that could suggest AI assistance
Differentiation is moderate—nothing particularly memorable or unique in the narrative
revision_suggestions: Add 2-3 outcome metrics to resume bullets: quantify impact (e.g., 'reduced document retrieval time by X%', 'improved accuracy by Y%', 'processed Z documents per day with N% error rate')
Tighten cover letter sentences to sound more conversational and less structured—break up the 40+ word sentences
Consider a brief acknowledgment that while biopharma is different from rehab therapy, the transferable skills include X, Y, Z specifically
Replace generic transition phrases like 'what drew me to' and 'maps closely to' with more direct, authentic language
Add one memorable detail or insight that would make this application stand out in a pile of 200
